prompt:

Asset type: one 16:9 editorial illustration for a personal portfolio case study about interior-design software and design-to-production workflows.
Primary request: show the SAME compact modern L-shaped kitchen in three coherent stages across one beautifully composed wide image: left a finished design concept; middle a structured, selectively exploded cabinet assembly revealing the carcasses, doors, shelves and countertop; right a drafting/workshop surface with clean orthographic plan/elevation sheets and a few matching cabinet panels and hardware. These are illustrative views of one kitchen, not product screenshots or engineering instructions.
Scene/backdrop: a seamless near-black velvet architectural studio, grounded tactile models on a shared dark work surface. The kitchen stays recognizable in all stages: warm natural oak lower cabinets, pale warm upper cabinets, cream stone counter, sink on the short run and cooktop on the long run.
Style/medium: sophisticated architectural model photography blended with precise 3D editorial rendering, credible wood grain, restrained physical construction detail, controlled depth and elegant negative space.
Composition/framing: landscape 16:9, eye-level three-quarter view, three equally readable stages from left to right, generous safe margins, no panel frames. Same camera orientation and cabinet layout between finished and exploded versions. Drafting papers are legible as drawings but contain no measurements or readable text. Keep large forms understandable at mobile size.
Lighting/mood: soft warm studio key, subtle cobalt edge accents, very sparse warm-gold connection marks; high enough brightness for clear inspection on a dark website.
Constraints: one image only; no people, robots, futuristic holograms, fake app UI, company branding, logos, titles, labels, words, numbers, watermarks, metrics, certification stamps or invented product claims. No giant glowing paths. Do not depict an actual client project. This is a conceptual editorial illustration with a separate website caption. Do not modify or reuse previous conversation images.
